## Background

I am an undergraduate researcher at Jeonbuk National University, majoring in
Statistics with a minor in Mathematics, and I am applying to PhD programs in
Statistics and Biostatistics.

I began in health data and have stayed close to it — clinical prediction from
electronic health records, and evidence synthesis from randomized trials — but
the questions that hold my attention are usually methodological rather than
clinical. Does a method still behave once its assumptions are loosened? Does a
result survive being carried into a different hospital, a different country, a
different population? Those questions are what took me from a meta-analysis of
dementia trials to neural Granger causality on meteorological series and on to
transfer learning for intensive-care prediction, which looks like a scattered
list until you notice that each one is asking whether a claim holds up outside
the setting that produced it.

## What I work with

Statistical methods for observational health data, machine learning applied to
clinical prediction, and the evaluation problems that come with both —
calibration, generalization, and the question of whether a reported gain is
signal or an artifact of how the data were collected. Alongside that, time
series and causal discovery, and spectral methods for community structure in
networks.

Details of the individual projects are on the [Research](research.qmd) page.
